All-Through Open Day Events
Our Open Events are the perfect opportunity to explore what makes our all-through school community so special – across Preston Manor Lower School, Upper School and Sixth Form.
Welcome to Preston Manor
Established in 1938, Preston Manor School is a thriving, inclusive all-through school serving its local community. It operates across two sites, with a Lower School (Reception to Year 6) and an Upper School (Year 7 to Sixth Form), supporting students throughout their entire educational journey.
The school has a committed staff and Governing Body alongside a supportive parent body. The school is known for strong academic performance, consistently exceeding national averages, and for its commitment to developing well-rounded individuals. With extensive outdoor space, students benefit from both academic and outdoor learning opportunities.
At its core, the school promotes three key values:
What makes our school special?
Our website is designed to help you know and understand more about the school. It cannot, however, tell the whole story. Please contact the school via email info@preston-manor.com or telephone 020 8385 4040, and we will be happy to help.

pageCache.text:
About Us
Our school is a vibrant, happy All-Through school where our young people join us in Reception and can stay with us all the way through until the end of Year 13. It is truly a unique experience that we have to offer and one that is centred on our strong partnership with our students and their families, realising each individual’s potential.
Our school is part of our community, and our community shares the pride that we have in our performance. We have consistently high performance in our public examinations as well as provide many opportunities outside the classroom to develop and nurture our young people as we prepare them for 21st Century society.
We are an inclusive school where every individual is valued and diversity is celebrated. We are committed to equality of opportunity, and we are rightly proud of our caring and nurturing ethos. Visitors to our school always comment on how warm, friendly and welcoming our school is.
At Preston Manor we seek to provide an education that enables our students to gain university places of their choice, the desire to continue lifelong learning, the skills needed to be successful in the workplace, and the ability to be emotionally aware. It is our ambition for students to leave us well-prepared to be active citizen of both today and the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Preston Manor - Welcome from the Head of Upper School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head of Upper School
I’m delighted to welcome you to Preston Manor Upper School. It is our firm belief that all students can be successful, irrespective of background or prior achievement, through high levels of teaching and pastoral support. GCSE results have been consistently positive for several years, giving our students great options for the next stages of their education.
As Headteacher of the Upper School, it is my role to create a safe environment where all students are ambitious about their future and to break down any barriers to learning. In living our values of Ambition, Responsibility and Excellence each day, the staff, students and parents will ensure the very highest of expectations are met in all that we do, ensuring that our young people go on to have great lives. We want our students to complete their whole education journey at Preston Manor by joining Reception in our Lower School and staying with us through Year 12 and Year 13 in our thriving Sixth Form. Since joining Preston Manor in September 2023, I have been taken aback by how warm and friendly a community it is, and I look forward to watching our students grow academically, culturally and confidently; able to pursue the careers they are passionate about and contribute positively to society. If you already have a child at our school, our website is a great source of information about all aspects of school life. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us by calling us on 020 8385 4040 or emailing us on info@preston-manor.com. We are proud to serve our community in Brent and are here to support you and your child every step of the way.
Mr. Tom Phillips Headteacher of Upper School

pageCache.text:
Our Values
We are a thriving All-Through school in Brent, and it is our aim to be an excellent and memorable school. We have the highest aspirations for all children, students and staff who are able to enjoy learning in a safe and inclusive environment.
We understand how important it is to work together as a community to help students enjoy their learning and achieve their best in all aspects of school life.
Ambition
We are ambitious for all of our students. Our ambition is driven through raising aspirations, our broad and balanced curriculum and the opportunities that are provided beyond the classroom. We want Preston Manor students to be active citizens, to be prepared for their future, to be happy, healthy and safe and caring individuals who are responsible learners. Students’ ambition and equality of opportunity enable them to achieve excellence. We achieve this through our PSHE, Citizenship, UCAS and careers programme which underpins our curriculum and high quality teaching and learning.
Responsibility
Students are encouraged to lead in their own learning and commit fully to their studies. All of our students have the responsibility to develop their own leadership skills from joining Reception to the end of their learning at school. We want our pupils to realise their dreams through a positive contribution to their community and wider society. We all have the responsibility to remove the barriers to each individual’s development and create the conditions in which our young people are able to love and enjoy learning inclusively. We achieve this through our student leadership, DIVA, Sporting, Artistic and Cultural opportunities embedding responsibility before rights - Munus Prae Jure.
Excellence
Driving our ambition and developing responsibility ensures that each individual achieves personal excellence at the end of every key stage. Our students leave their learning journey at our school with excellent values, virtue, integrity and high academic and personal outcomes. We are making school memorable by striving for excellence.
We ‘ARE’ Preston Manor School.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from Head Students
We are delighted to introduce to you our Head Boy and Head Girl of both Lower and Upper School.
Lower School Head Students
Upper School Head Students
My journey in student leadership started early. In Year 7, I was recognised with a Jack Petchey Award for being a strong role model and lead learner in Maths and PE – an experience that motivated me to stay active in school life. Over the years, I have served on the School Council, worked as a high school Prefect, become a member of the Eco Manor Club, and also a Senior Prefect. Entering Sixth Form accelerated my personal and academic growth through exciting new opportunities. Alongside my studies, the school gave me the platform to pursue my creative passions, including memorable experiences taking part in national sporting competitions and work experiences at major companies. Being appointed Head Student is an incredible honour. Having been a part of this incredible community from a young age all the way to Year 13, I now want to use this position to solve problems in our school as well as set up amazing events to bring everyone together. As I enter my final year at Preston Manor, taking on the role of Head Student is a heartfelt commitment. This school has been my second home for fourteen years. I am dedicated to representing our unique all-through community and giving back to the place that has shaped my life.
My journey in leadership began in Year 7, when I was fortunate enough to receive the Jack Petchey Award. Since then, I have taken on increasing responsibility, becoming a Prefect in Year 11, a Senior Prefect in Year 12, and now Head Boy. These experiences have taught me that leadership is not about having the loudest voice, but about listening to others, supporting those around you and being someone people can rely on.
I have also always tried to make the most of the opportunities beyond the classroom. My curiosity has led me to pursue my own interests independently, including researching Neanderthal and Homo sapiens introgression and presenting my work independently to Queen Mary University of London. This taught me the importance of stepping outside my comfort zone, asking questions and pursuing opportunities beyond what is expected of me.
As Head Boy, I want to help create a school where every student feels heard, supported and confident in what they can achieve. I want to be approachable and present, whether that means representing students, supporting younger pupils or celebrating their successes.
I am incredibly grateful for the opportunities this school has given me, and I hope that during my time as Head Boy, I can give something meaningful back and help inspire others to make the most of every opportunity available to them.
One thing I have learnt throughout my time here is that there is so much on offer if you are willing to take the opportunities presented to you. I have been fortunate to have teachers who have constantly encouraged me to step outside my comfort zone, whether academically, through leadership, or through experiences beyond school. Staff such as Ms Wilding has continuously introduced us to opportunities that I may never have discovered independently, including work experience with organisations such as Markel.
Some of the experiences that have meant the most to me have been those that allowed me to support and encourage others. Through D.I.V.A., I have had the opportunity to help other girls develop their confidence and prepare themselves for the workplace and their future endeavours. Being able to encourage other students to recognise their own potential has made this experience particularly meaningful to me.
Preston Manor has also encouraged me to find my own voice. One of my proudest achievements was winning the Brent regional Jack Petchey Speak Out Challenge. Standing on a stage and speaking confidently in front of others showed me just how much I had grown. From becoming a Prefect and Senior Prefect to competing in public speaking, each experience has pushed me beyond what I thought I was capable of and helped me become more confident in representing others.
Now, as Head Student, I want to use that confidence to create opportunities for other students. Alongside the other Head Students, I want to strengthen the sense of community that has made Preston Manor so important to me. Whether through our plans to raise money to fund a well for a community in need, creating spaces for students to discuss world issues through our debate club, or simply making sure students feel that their voices are heard, I want my time as Head Student to have a positive impact.
For me, Preston Manor has always been more than what happens inside the classroom. It is the people who support you, the experiences that challenge you and the opportunities that can take you somewhere you never expected.
After fourteen years, this community has given me an incredible amount. As Head Student, I am proud to have the opportunity to represent it, contribute to it, and hopefully encourage other students to take every opportunity that comes their way.
- Naa Afia (Year 13)

Welcome from the Head of Lower School
I am privileged to lead the primary section of Preston Manor School. I take huge pride in seeing how wonderfully kind and friendly the children become. Being an all-through school, we have the unique ability to maintain our relationships with our children and families all the way through to the Sixth Form.
This gives our children and their families a unique advantage over all other primary schools, as you and your child have already built an excellent relationship with us which is maintained throughout their school career. The transition between primary and secondary is almost seamless for our children as they have experienced the Upper School site, staff and students regularly throughout their primary journey.
At Preston Manor Lower School we believe that children’s success is built on excellent relationships, an inclusive curriculum which children can see themselves represented in, an inclusive learning environment and learning that is practical and full of memorable experiences. We have very high expectations and our children and our children have high expectations of themselves. This has led to significantly improved outcomes for our children.
We believe in creating leaders at Preston Manor School, and we provide the children with many and varied leadership opportunities. These opportunities allow our children to develop their leadership skills amongst their peers and fellow pupils but also through their interactions with their peers in the Upper School. These opportunities are invaluable in producing confident and competent children who are able to communicate with a wide variety of people.
Lastly, we believe that children will be most successful if there is a strong partnership between home and school. As partners, we share the responsibility for our children’s success and want you to know that we will do our very best to carry out our responsibilities. Welcome from Head of Sixth Form
A very warm welcome to our Sixth Form. I am both proud and privileged to be the Head of Sixth Form at Preston Manor School. With over 18 years of proven success, our A-level results regularly place us amongst the top performing schools nationally for value-added at Key Stage 5. So, no matter your starting point, you will make excellent progress here with us.
Our destination measures are also second to none. A very high percentage of our able cohort gain places at Russell group and GOLD standard universities, as well as our country's top research institutions, including Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial and UCL. They go on to study courses such as Law, Engineering, Medicine, Pharmacy and Dentistry.
Choosing to join the Preston Manor Sixth Form means that you are joining a successful community of Post 16 learners. Learners are challenged, supported and encouraged to achieve their very best.
At Preston Manor School, you will find welcoming students, supportive teachers and committed pastoral teams at the heart of our community. Whether you are an existing Preston Manor student or currently studying elsewhere, I hope you can see the many benefits of joining our high-achieving sixth form and I look forward to receiving your application.
Ms. Catherine Snoad Assistant Headteacher/Head of Sixth Form

Parent Engagment
The Parent Partnership Group Meetings at Preston Manor is a remote initiative that works hard to engage parents in ideas and strategies to ultimately help to raise students' achievement.
There is a small Parent's Focus Group that meets to discuss potential agendas for the Partnership group meetings. Both the Partnership and the Focus group cover all key stages, and recently replaced the Parent Association format.
The revised parent partnership structure will have approximately 2 meetings a term. Prior to these meetings, all parents will be asked to complete a survey beforehand. Themes within the survey will change each time, and reflect the issues at the time.
The Parent Partnership is a valued forum for parents/carers to share initiatives and discuss concerns with invited and key members of the school community. Importantly, the parent partnership works to both engage and inform our parents/carers.
Forthcoming meetings via Zoom
Please email Ms. Zalika Dale: z.dale@preston-manor.com if you would like to send a message to the Parent Partnership, or would like to raise issues that you think would be useful to discuss at our next meeting.
PLEASE NOTE : If you require documents to be interpreted or translated for clarity, please do not hesitate to bring this to the attention of the Assistant Headteacher – Ms. Zalika Dale. We will endeavour to ensure that all communications are understood by all families.

Parent View
Parent View is an online survey that allows parents to give their views about their child’s school. By ‘parents’, we mean any person with parental responsibility for a child at the school.
Parents can complete the survey at any time. It is also the main mechanism for parents to give their views to inspectors at the time of a school inspection.
The survey can be accessed directly from the Ofsted Parent View site or from the homepage of Ofsted website.
We encourage parents to use Ofsted Parent View to give views on our school either during an inspection or at any other time of the year.
Leading Parent Partnership Award
The school is proud to have been awarded the Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA)
This is a national award that provides a coherent framework through which schools, early years settings and other educational organisations can deliver effective parental engagement from early years to post-16.

Upper School Curriculum
At Preston Manor, we envision a thriving educational community where every student, regardless of background, is empowered to achieve excellence. We are committed to providing an exceptional education that surpasses national standards, ensuring that every student not only meets but exceeds their targets. Through our rigorous curriculum and five Teaching and Learning Principles, we nurture a culture of ambition, responsibility and excellence.
Our dedicated teachers are experts in their subject and are committed to improving their practice through professional development and pertinent reading. They take responsibility for meeting the needs of all students, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Leaders at all levels are actively involved in monitoring the implementation of our curriculum to ensure it impacts positively on students’ outcomes. We nurture a culture of intellectual curiosity, setting up consistent homework to develop independent and responsible learners. Our rigorous assessment system helps us track student progress and refine our academic curriculum. We celebrate our students’ self-worth in every lesson, fostering a learning environment where they can speak eloquently, write with clarity and read extensively.
Together, we ARE dedicated to developing the leaders, thinkers and innovators of tomorrow.

Music Academy
The Preston Manor Music Academy is a Saturday community music school based at the School. It caters to children from Year 2 to Year 13. The Music Academy has won five major awards, including the first ever Mayor of London’s Music Excellence in Schools Award, Roland’s Champion School for Music Status and the ABRSM’s Music Mark.
The Music Academy not only offers its students the chance to learn an instrument but also the opportunity to play in an ensemble, sing and learn the theory of music. The study of music theory enables children to gain a greater appreciation of the pieces they may be learning in their instrumental lessons and a more thorough understanding of classroom-based music activities through all the key stages. Over the last twenty-plus years, the Music Academy has had many successes in both practical (including Grade 8) and theoretical music examinations from the full range of examination providers.
Students attending the Music Academy may choose to learn the piano, keyboard, drum kit, classical or electric guitar, bass guitar, ukulele saxophone, flute and violin. These are all taught in small groups of between 3 and 4 students.
Staff and Roles
Head of Performing Arts, General Musicianship, Music Theory, Ensemble
Saxophone, Keyboard, Piano, Music Theory
Violin, Music Theory

Drum Kit, Keyboard, Piano, Music Theory
Mr P. Guglielminotti
The Music Academy collaborates with English National Opera, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, Brent Music Service, Old School Assembly and universities, including the UCL Institute of Education.
Every year, the Music Academy puts on a Christmas sharing as well as a spring and summer concert in which pupils play a wide range of instruments, both solo and in groups.
As we aim to rebuild our provision following the pandemic, the Music Academy is currently staffed by a team of 6 professional musicians that are not only teachers but are also working in the music industry as musicians who run their own recording studios, music production companies, sing and play in professional choruses, orchestras and chamber ensembles alongside teaching and further academic studies.

Music Development Plan
Music sits within the faculty of Performing Arts, which works to inspire and promote both acceptance and awareness in all students.
We aim to foster a lifelong passion for music whilst ensuring all students have access to experiences both in school and our wider community that develop personal growth, confidence, and analytical thinking. Participation is at the heart of all we do; fostering creativity, enhancing communication skills and teamwork, which enables students to express themselves confidently in music alongside a range of artistic forms including drama and dance. By exploring our diverse cultures, histories, and genres, we encourage students to enrich their cultural capital within both music and the performing arts as a whole.
Below you will find a summary of how our school delivers music education to all our students across three areas – curriculum music, co-curricular provision and musical experiences – and what changes we are planning in future years.
This information is to help pupils and parents or carers understand what our school offers and who we work with to support our students’ music education.
